'''Horng-Tzer Yau''' ({{zh|t=姚鴻澤|p=Yáo Hóngzé}}; born June 29, 1959) is a Taiwanese-American mathematician who is the Merton Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]].

== Early life and education ==
Yau was born in 1959 in Taiwan, where he began studying advanced calculus and college algebra in high school.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brustman |first=Bob |date=2006-03-02 |title=Yau travels down the road less taken |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2006/03/yau-travels-down-the-road-less-taken/ |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=Harvard Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref> He graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in 1981. As an undergraduate, he studied [[differential geometry]], [[real analysis]], and [[complex analysis]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Liu |first=Tai-ping |date=August 2001 |title=An Interview with Professor Yao Hongze |url=https://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/media/pdf/d273/27302.pdf |access-date=28 February 2026 |publisher=[[Academia Sinica]] |language=zh-TW}}</ref> After graduation, he served two years of military service in the [[Republic of China Armed Forces]] from 1981 to 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |title=浙江大学数学研究中心 |url=http://www.cms.zju.edu.cn/index.php?a=member&id=412 |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=www.cms.zju.edu.cn}}</ref>

In 1987, Yau earned his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from [[Princeton University]]. His doctoral dissertation, completed under mathematical physicist [[Elliott Lieb]], was titled, "Stability of Coulomb Systems".<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=30832|name=Horng-Tzer Yau}}</ref> After receiving his doctorate, Yao completed [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] under [[David Brydges]] from 1987 to 1988.<ref name=":0" />
== Academic career ==
In 1988, Yau joined the mathematics faculty at [[New York University]]. He became a full professor at its [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] in 1994. He then moved to [[Stanford University]] in 2003, and then to [[Harvard University]] in 2005. He was also a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey, in 2003, and was a distinguished visiting professor there in 2013–14.<ref>{{cite web|title=Horng-Tzer Yau|website=Institute for Advanced Study (ias.edu)|date=December 9, 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/horng-tzer-yau}}</ref>
 
According to [[William C. Kirby]],  dean of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences at Harvard, "Professor Yau is a leader in the fields of [[mathematical physics]],  ...  who has introduced important tools and concepts to study probability, stochastic processes, nonequilibrium statistical physics, and quantum dynamics."<ref>[http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/2005/04.14/19-yau.html Harvard University Gazette] April 14, 2005</ref>

Yau is a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|2000 MacArthur Fellow]].
